records.title: Concern over recent landslides and natural calamities in Mizoram
details:
Shri Khiangte Laltluangkima:
I seek to draw? attention of the Government to
the serious situation arising from repeated landslides and other rain-related
disasters across Mizoram during the current monsoon. More than 100 major
calamity incidents, including around 74 landslides, besides rockfalls, storms,
land subsidence, retaining-wall collapses and mudflow, have been reported
across the State. Khawzawl alone has reported about 30 landslides. Numerous
smaller landslides have also occurred across towns and localities. These
incidents have repeatedly disrupted vital road connectivity. Major landslides
along NH-54A in Lunglei stranded travellers and damaged houses, while recurring
rockfalls at Ngaizel in Aizawl threaten a vital road serving southern Mizoram
and two major hospitals. In Serchhip, 143 families and houses were affected,
while a major hailstorm in Mamit affected 198 families and houses. The State
Government, DDMAs, SDRF, PWD, BRO/BRTF, NHIDCL and local communities are
continuously undertaking relief, evacuation and road restoration. I urge the
Government to provide financial and technical assistance for permanent
slope stabilisation, retaining structures, drainage, rockfall protection,
early-warning systems and adequate road-clearance machinery through SDRF/SDMF
and other appropriate mechanisms. Mizoram needs a long-term landslide
mitigation and resilient-infrastructure programme to protect its people and
lifeline connectivity. 
(ENDS)
